title: Concerted TTFT surge: investigate queued priming lag across hosting tiers
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers (two Dedicated tenants and three Hosted accounts) reported sudden increases in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and degraded tokens/sec for multimodal and long-context models over the last 48 hours. The anomaly crosses Hosted / Dedicated / Private stacks, appears at model fanout points, and correlates with increased queued priming time and slow priming completion for frequently‑used prompt prefixes.

Scope: Impact observed for rw-long-1.0 and open-compat/llama-large-quant variants across regions us-west-2 and eu-central. Symptoms include TTFT regressions from baseline ~120ms to sustained 500–900ms for first token and throughput reductions ~30% on multiplexed routes. Customers reported visible UX hitches and increased API timeouts.

Initial Triage: Alerts fired on the platform SLO dashboard (TTFT p95 and p99); traces show long wait times in the priming queue before the worker handshake. Kernel execution times unchanged. Prefetch/KV cache hit rates were stable but priming queue length spiked concurrent with a cross-region deployment of a routing change made 36 hours prior.

Hypothesis: A routing heuristic change inadvertently increased serialized priming for warmup paths when fanout > 3 and model variants flagged as "compat-fallback". This caused head-of-line priming delays in multiplex queues that propagate downstream as TTFT spikes.

Goals: 1) Mitigate customer impact with an immediate lightweight rollback or circuit to avoid serialized priming; 2) Fully root-cause and harden routing and multiplex queue prioritization so similar fanout patterns do not reintroduce the issue; 3) Provide a clear postmortem and customer communication plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route 12 concurrent requests with shared prefix to a multiplexed host serving rw-long-1.0 + llama-large-quant fallback
2) Observe p95 TTFT via tracing and Grafana over a 10 minute window
3) Simulate routing policy 'compat-fallback-fanout' to force serialized priming on warm workers
mitigation_tasks: 1) Toggle routing flag 'compat-fallback-serial' -> off (hot config) to allow parallel priming
2) Temporarily increase multiplex worker pool for affected hosts in us-west-2 and eu-central
3) Apply short-term rate-cap for canary-tier customers to reduce head-of-line blocking
4) Deploy quick telemetry probe to surface priming queue lengths and head latency per-model
